findings.reason: The approved BCS-17 design includes the IID density weak BvM for Type-S/Type-H priors under the stated cutoffs and truth conditions. The A-page objective explicitly excludes that source-specific result, and no assigned item proves it.

The theorem's premise (i) is not established for either Type-S or Type-H priors. The BCS-08 contraction theorem requires entropy and prior-mass conditions that are not verified here and does not supply the needed multiscale posterior BvM. Castillo–Nickl (2014), Theorem 3 and §5.4, requires posterior concentration on D_n, restricted exponential-moment bounds, and finite-dimensional density BvM limits; its Type-H shift argument is deferred there. The smallest missing prerequisite is the Type-S/Type-H posterior weak BvM in M0(w), under the approved conditions. See the [primary source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1310.2484), §5.4, printed pp. 23–28.

Steps 1.1–1.2 use the continuous mapping theorem to obtain weak convergence, but then apply the quantile lemma, which requires bounded-Lipschitz convergence. Supply the direct Lipschitz pushforward bound for J and the norm maps. Step 1.1 also identifies the covariance of J#G without stating why the continuous linear image of the Gaussian law G is Gaussian.
